findings.title: No immutable audit logging for write operations
findings.description: No immutable audit logging configured. Write operations do not log the authenticated principal. The deleteProduct resolver acknowledges this gap in a code comment.
findings.gap: No immutable, tamper-evident audit trail recording which principal performed each write operation. No CloudTrail configuration. No application-level audit event emission on mutations.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudTrail configuration with log file validation and S3 bucket with object lock. Emit structured audit events from mutation resolvers capturing JWT sub claim, action, and timestamp.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled requires immutable audit trail for all write operations.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: AUTH-Q6 resolved to BLOCKER because agent_scope is write-enabled and the service exposes upsertProduct and deleteProduct mutations without any audit logging of the authenticated principal.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add CloudTrail resource to infra/template.yaml with log file validation enabled and S3 bucket with object lock.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Every write operation produces an immutable audit record identifying the authenticated principal, action performed, affected resource (SKU), and timestamp.

findings.title: No identity propagation or agent-vs-user distinction
findings.description: JWT claims are extracted from the API Gateway authorizer context. However, there is no mechanism to distinguish between an agent acting under its own identity vs. acting on behalf of a user.
findings.gap: No on-behalf-of flow or token exchange pattern. No code logic differentiating agent-as-self from agent-on-behalf-of-user.
findings.recommendation: Implement separate Cognito app clients for agent vs user callers with custom claims for actor type differentiation.

compensating_controls: Configure separate Cognito app clients for agent vs user identities
Add custom JWT claim for actor type differentiation

findings.title: No concurrency controls on write operations
findings.description: No optimistic locking or concurrency controls. upsertProduct uses unconditional db.put() — last-write-wins with no version field or conditional expression.
findings.gap: No version field, no ETag, no DynamoDB conditional writes. Multiple concurrent agents writing to the same SKU will silently overwrite each other.
findings.recommendation: Add a version field and DynamoDB ConditionExpression to detect concurrent modification. Return a conflict error when the condition fails.

compensating_controls: Add version-based conditional writes to DynamoDB
Limit concurrent agent instances to 1 per SKU

findings.title: No per-client rate limiting configured
findings.description: The SAM HttpApi does not configure explicit throttling. No per-client rate limiting, no WAF rate rules, no usage plan.
findings.gap: Runaway agent loop not throttled beyond account-wide API Gateway defaults (10,000 req/s).
findings.recommendation: Add API Gateway throttle configuration per route and per client. Deploy WAF WebACL with rate-based rules.

compensating_controls: Add API Gateway usage plan with per-API-key throttle
Deploy WAF rate-based rules

findings.title: No business transaction limits per agent identity
findings.description: No configurable transaction limits. Each mutation affects one record but no cap on total mutations per session or per hour per agent identity.
findings.gap: No per-session or per-identity business transaction limits. An agent could loop and modify all products rapidly.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-identity mutation counters in DynamoDB with configurable thresholds per time window.

compensating_controls: Implement per-identity mutation counters with thresholds
Add orchestration-layer limit at agent framework level

findings.title: No draft/pending state for agent-proposed changes
findings.description: No draft or pending state concept. upsertProduct immediately commits. deleteProduct immediately soft-deletes. No intermediate state for human review.
findings.gap: All mutations are immediately effective. Agents cannot propose changes for human review before committing.
findings.recommendation: Add a status enum field (DRAFT, ACTIVE) to the product schema. Agent-initiated mutations create products in DRAFT status.

compensating_controls: Add status field with DRAFT/ACTIVE states
Implement approval workflow at agent orchestration layer

findings.title: No configurable approval gates for mutations
findings.description: No approval gate mechanism. All mutations execute immediately when the caller has catalog:write scope. No configurable flag to require human confirmation.
findings.gap: No operation-level approval configuration. No Step Functions with human approval tasks.
findings.recommendation: Add Step Functions approval workflow for deleteProduct using waitForTaskToken for human confirmation.

compensating_controls: Wrap high-risk mutations in Step Function with human approval
Implement orchestration-layer approval gates

findings.title: No structured error code taxonomy
findings.description: Apollo Server provides GraphQL-standard error responses but no custom error code taxonomy distinguishing retriable from terminal errors.
findings.gap: No error code taxonomy. Agents cannot programmatically distinguish retriable from terminal errors without parsing message strings.
findings.recommendation: Add custom GraphQLError subclasses with extensions.code values (FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, RATE_LIMITED) and retryable boolean.

compensating_controls: Use Apollo extensions.code for machine-readable error codes
Document error codes in schema description

findings.title: Incomplete temporal metadata and no freshness signaling
findings.description: Products have updatedAt field (UTC ISO 8601) but no createdAt timestamp. No freshness signaling to agents (no Cache-Control headers, no data-age indicators).
findings.gap: Missing createdAt field. No mechanism for agents to determine data currency.
findings.recommendation: Add createdAt to Product type. Consider adding freshness response headers or envelope fields.

compensating_controls: Add createdAt field on initial insert
Add response metadata indicating data freshness

findings.title: No breaking change detection for schema
findings.description: GraphQL schema is schema-first and version-controlled but no breaking change detection in CI, no consumer-driven contract tests.
findings.gap: Schema changes could break agent tool bindings without early detection. No schema diff tooling.
findings.recommendation: Integrate graphql-inspector or similar schema diff tool into CI to flag breaking changes before merge.

compensating_controls: Add graphql-inspector to CI
Pin agent tool definitions to schema hash

findings.title: No sandbox/staging environment for agent testing
findings.description: No staging or sandbox environment configuration. No docker-compose, no seed data, no environment-specific configs.
findings.gap: No safe environment for testing agent behavior before production.
findings.recommendation: Add docker-compose with DynamoDB Local and seed data for local agent testing. Create samconfig.toml with staging profile.

compensating_controls: Deploy SAM stack with separate staging parameters
Add docker-compose with DynamoDB Local

findings.title: No structured logging with correlation IDs
findings.description: X-Ray active tracing enabled for distributed tracing. No structured JSON logging implemented in application code. No correlation ID propagation.
findings.gap: Application-level structured logs with correlation IDs missing. Only X-Ray trace-level visibility.
findings.recommendation: Add @aws-lambda-powertools/logger for structured JSON logging with automatic correlation ID and X-Ray trace ID propagation.

compensating_controls: X-Ray provides request-level tracing as partial mitigation
Add structured logger with correlation IDs

findings.title: No alerting configured for API degradation
findings.description: No CloudWatch alarms configured in the SAM template. No alerting thresholds for error rates or latency.
findings.gap: API degradation will not trigger notifications. No proactive detection of agent-impacting issues.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms for Lambda error count, duration P99, and API Gateway 5xx rate.

compensating_controls: Add CloudWatch alarms for Lambda errors and duration
Configure API Gateway 4xx/5xx alarms

findings.title: IaC present but no review workflow or drift detection
findings.description: Infrastructure defined as code in SAM template. No CI/CD pipeline enforces peer review. No drift detection configured.
findings.gap: Two of three governance sub-checks unmet: no automated plan review and no drift detection.
findings.recommendation: Add CI pipeline with sam validate and changeset review. Enable AWS Config rules for drift detection.

compensating_controls: Add CI pipeline for template validation
Enable AWS Config drift detection

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline or contract testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline configuration in repository. No contract tests or schema validation in builds.
findings.gap: No automated pipeline. Schema changes not validated before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Create CI pipeline with TypeScript compilation, vitest, and graphql-inspector on every PR.

compensating_controls: Add minimal CI pipeline for build and test
Implement pre-deploy schema validation gate

findings.title: No rollback capability configured
findings.description: No deployment preference or rollback configuration. No canary, no blue/green, no automatic rollback triggers.
findings.gap: Broken deployment requires manual intervention to restore service.
findings.recommendation: Add AutoPublishAlias and DeploymentPreference with Canary10Percent5Minutes and alarm-based rollback.

compensating_controls: Add DeploymentPreference with canary and alarm rollback
CloudFormation stack rollback on failure as baseline

findings.title: Zero test coverage for API endpoints
findings.description: Test framework configured (vitest in package.json) but no test files exist in the repository.
findings.gap: No automated tests. API behavior changes cannot be caught before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Create resolver integration tests with DynamoDB mocks covering query, mutation, auth, and error cases.

compensating_controls: Add integration tests for resolvers with mock DynamoDB
Add schema-level tests for query/mutation responses

findings.title: Not a sensitive data handling target
findings.description: System stores product catalog data (SKU, name, price, currency, active status). Not PII, PHI, financial instruments, or credentials. Stage A = No.
findings.gap: N/A — not a data-handling target for sensitive data concerns.
findings.recommendation: Re-evaluate if the service evolves to store user-specific data.

findings.title: No event emission on state changes
findings.description: No event emission on state changes. No SNS/EventBridge/SQS integration. No DynamoDB Streams configured.
findings.gap: State changes are not observable by external consumers without polling.
findings.recommendation: Enable DynamoDB Streams and publish change events to EventBridge.

findings.title: Rate limits not documented or configured
findings.description: No rate limit documentation or headers. No API Gateway usage plan or throttle documentation.
findings.gap: Agents have no visibility into rate limit status.
findings.recommendation: Document rate limits in schema and add rate limit headers via API Gateway.

findings.title: No data quality metrics or monitoring
findings.description: No data quality metrics, profiling, or completeness monitoring for the products table.
findings.gap: No quality signal for agent consumers of catalog data.
findings.recommendation: Add periodic data quality check monitoring null rates and record completeness.

findings.title: No custom business outcome metrics
findings.description: No custom business metrics published. Only infrastructure-level metrics from Lambda/API Gateway defaults.
findings.gap: Cannot measure business outcomes of agent-initiated catalog operations.
findings.recommendation: Add custom CloudWatch metrics for catalog operations using @aws-lambda-powertools/metrics.

evaluations.title: Documented API Interface
evaluations.reason: GraphQL interface exposed via Apollo Server 4 with schema-first design. Machine-discoverable via introspection.

evaluations.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
evaluations.reason: GraphQL schema (schema/catalog.graphql) is inherently machine-readable with runtime introspection.

evaluations.title: Idempotent Write Operations
evaluations.reason: All writes are idempotent: upsertProduct is a PutItem keyed by SKU, deleteProduct is a repeatable soft-delete.

evaluations.title: Structured Response Format
evaluations.reason: GraphQL returns structured JSON responses by default. All queries and mutations return typed JSON objects.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no operations exceed 30s, no long-running workflows. All DynamoDB operations complete in milliseconds.

evaluations.title: Machine Identity Authentication
evaluations.reason: Cognito JWT authorizer on API Gateway supports machine identity via client credentials with audience and scope-based attribution.

evaluations.title: Scoped Permissions
evaluations.reason: JWT scopes differentiate access: catalog:write required for mutations, read open to any authenticated client. IAM role scoped to specific table.

evaluations.title: Action-Level Authorization
evaluations.reason: requireScope check enforces action-level auth — read-only clients can query but not mutate within the same resource type.

evaluations.title: Credential Management
evaluations.reason: No hardcoded credentials. Lambda uses IAM roles. UserPoolId is a CloudFormation parameter.

evaluations.title: Agent Identity Suspension
evaluations.reason: Cognito user pool supports disabling individual users/app clients for identity suspension without platform-wide impact.

evaluations.title: Compensation and Rollback
evaluations.reason: No multi-step write workflows exist. All operations are atomic single-record DynamoDB calls. Deletes are reversible (soft-delete).

evaluations.title: Queryable Current State
evaluations.reason: product(sku) and products(limit, cursor) queries allow agents to inspect current state before acting.

evaluations.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — service only calls DynamoDB via AWS SDK (built-in retry logic). No external service dependencies.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no priority specified, service not identified as critical path.

evaluations.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
evaluations.reason: Data stored is product catalog metadata (SKU, name, price, currency) — not regulated personal data. No residency constraints.

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Cursor-based pagination with configurable limit. GraphQL field selection. Single-product lookup by SKU.

evaluations.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
evaluations.reason: GraphQL schema enforces type-level validation with non-null fields. Apollo Server returns structured validation errors.

evaluations.title: PII Redaction in Logs
evaluations.reason: System handles product catalog data only (SKU, name, price). No PII in the system — PII cannot leak into logs.

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: All field names are clear and semantically meaningful: sku, name, priceCents, currency, active, updatedAt. No legacy abbreviations.

evaluations.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
evaluations.reason: GraphQL schema with descriptions serves as self-describing metadata layer. Introspection makes all types discoverable at runtime.

evaluations.title: Encryption at Rest
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB SSESpecification enabled (SSEEnabled: true). Point-in-time recovery also enabled.

items.summary: Resolve the audit logging BLOCKER and address critical safety risks: concurrency controls, rate limiting, and human-in-the-loop mechanisms.
Address remaining safety risks (identity propagation, transaction limits) and quality gaps (error codes, observability, CI/CD, rollback).
Improve test coverage, add event emission, document rate limits, and publish business metrics.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy immutable audit logging for write operations
recommended_actions.rationale: BLOCKER: Required before any agent deployment. Add CloudTrail with log validation and application-level audit events on mutations.

recommended_actions.action: Add API Gateway throttling and rate limits
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents runaway agent loops from overwhelming the service. Quick win via API Gateway configuration.

recommended_actions.action: Implement optimistic locking on DynamoDB writes
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents data corruption from concurrent agent instances operating on the same SKU.
Enables human oversight for agent-initiated catalog changes. Defense-in-depth for write operations.

recommended_actions.action: Build CI/CD pipeline with schema validation
recommended_actions.rationale: Establishes engineering maturity: automated testing, breaking change detection, and safe deployments.
Enables debugging of agent-initiated requests and proactive detection of service degradation.
